title: AI-ConneX Three Studios Independence and Microservice Modularity
summary: Microservice modularity contracts decoupling Data Studio, ML Studio, and Agentic Studio with asynchronous REST/gRPC interfaces.

sections.content:
AI-ConneX

THREE-STUDIO INDEPENDENCE & MICROSERVICE MODULARITY

Data Studio • ML Studio • Agentic StudioArchitecture Proof • Modular Contracts • Deployment Models • POCVersion 1.0 | 14 August 2026

AI-ConneX can be architected as three independently deployable Studios rather than one inseparable application. Independence means each Studio owns a bounded capability, its release lifecycle, APIs, storage boundaries and operational SLOs. Integration happens through explicit contracts—Manifest/Artifact IDs, REST/gRPC APIs, event streams and versioned schemas—not by importing internal code or directly sharing databases.

This is a stronger fit for industrial customers because a factory can consume Data Studio for data organization and visualization without buying ML, consume ML Studio only when predictive modeling is needed, or consume Agentic Studio as an automation/operations layer. The complete AI-ConneX platform remains available when all three are joined.

This architecture follows established cloud-native guidance: loosely coupled components with well-defined responsibilities are easier to scale and change independently. CNCF describes cloud-native software as loosely coupled, resilient, manageable and observable, and notes that microservices handle well-defined tasks. citeturn0search0turn0search10

Independence does not mean zero dependencies. It means dependencies are externalized as stable contracts. A Studio may consume another Studio's artifact/API without becoming structurally dependent on its implementation.
tables:
| Studio | Independent product capability | Can operate without |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data Studio | Ingest → compile → profile → DAG → prepare → feature engineer → visualize/serve organized data | ML Studio, Agentic Studio |
| ML Studio | Clean validation → DAG/family selection → split/train/evaluate → judge/score → model artifact | Agentic Studio; Data Studio runtime may be optional if input already satisfies contracts |
| Agentic Studio | Agent SPEC → runtime → RAG/KG → tools → main agent/toolkit → operational automation | ML Studio; Data Studio, provided required data/tool contracts exist |

sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-021 > 3. Why This Is Actually Possible
sections.content:
The proof is architectural: each Studio has a distinct bounded context, can expose a network/API boundary, can package its runtime independently, can persist its own state, and can consume immutable artifacts through contracts. The Twelve-Factor methodology explicitly treats backing services as attached resources and separates build, release and run. CNCF's modern interpretation also emphasizes independent components, APIs and automated deployment. citeturn0search1turn0search7

ONNX Runtime strengthens the ML independence claim because an approved model can be packaged as a portable inference artifact and executed across cloud, edge and other hardware environments without requiring the original training framework at serving time. citeturn0search2turn0search8

AI-ConneX Platform│├── DATA STUDIO│   └── Data Intelligence / Organization Boundary│├── ML STUDIO│   └── Model Intelligence / Prediction Boundary│└── AGENTIC STUDIO    └── Automation / Decision-Orchestration BoundaryShared Platform Contracts├── Identity / Tenant├── Manifest & Artifact IDs├── API/Event contracts├── Telemetry├── Policy└── Release / Deployment

The shared layer should contain contracts and platform services, not Studio-specific business logic. This prevents the shared layer from becoming a hidden monolith.

If a customer provides an already-clean, feature-ready dataset satisfying ML Studio's input contract, ML Studio can operate without running Data Studio. If the dataset does not satisfy the contract, Jane can recommend Data Studio; that is a service dependency at the workflow level, not a code dependency.

The serving artifact can be packaged independently. ONNX Runtime supports inference from models originating in multiple frameworks and across cloud, edge and mobile environments. citeturn0search2turn0search3

Agentic Studio therefore does not require ML Studio. It can operate on deterministic rules, data services, APIs and tools. Conversely, when an ML model exists, Agentic Studio can consume it through the model's inference contract.
This matrix is the key commercial proof: AI-ConneX is a platform of composable products, not a forced all-or-nothing suite.

Semantic versioning and compatibility rules should be applied to APIs and artifact schemas. A Studio can evolve independently when it preserves its published contract.

| Scenario | Allowed? | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |

sections.content:
Consumers declare the contract version they support.

Provider maintains N and N-1 compatibility for a defined window.

Breaking changes use a new API/schema version.

Adapters translate old contracts where necessary.

Release gates test consumer/provider compatibility.

Manifest references immutable versions.

/v1/data/compile/v2/data/compileschema_version: "1.2"contract_compatibility: ["1.0","1.1","1.2"]
This is the operational meaning of modularity: a failure in one bounded context should not automatically become a platform-wide outage.
tables:
| Failure | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Data Studio down | Existing ML model and Agentic runtime continue if their inputs are already available |
| ML Studio down | Data Studio continues; Agentic Studio continues with non-ML capabilities |
| Agentic Studio down | Data/ML services continue |
| MQTT broker down | Local buffering/degraded mode where applicable |
| One model fails | Other ML services remain available |
| One agent tool fails | Agent run isolates tool failure and applies fallback policy |

sections.content: Cloud-native architecture benefits from scaling services according to their own workload rather than scaling an entire monolith. CNCF describes service components as individually scalable and operationally manageable. citeturn0search0
tables:
| Workload | Scale independently |
| --- | --- |
| Data compilation | CPU/storage-heavy workers |
| Data visualization | GPU/CPU and session workers |
| Model training | GPU/CPU job workers |
| Model inference | Low-latency replicas/edge accelerators |
| Agent runtime | Concurrency/latency-driven replicas |
| RAG retrieval | Vector search capacity |
| Knowledge Graph | Graph query capacity |

sections.content:
Each Studio can have an edge profile. Data Studio may run fully at a plant to organize and visualize data. ML Studio can deploy an ONNX inference service at the edge without shipping the training environment. Agentic Studio can run a constrained local toolkit with approved tools and cached knowledge.

ONNX Runtime supports multiple execution providers and hardware environments, allowing the same model-serving contract to target CPU, GPU and specialized accelerators subject to model/provider compatibility. citeturn0search8

CNCF's edge-native guidance specifically calls out edge autonomy, capability sensitivity, data persistence, metrics/logs and edge operations as distinct design concerns. citeturn0search6

The same services can be deployed in Kubernetes or equivalent cloud infrastructure. The platform layer supplies ingress, identity, secrets, service discovery, autoscaling, observability and release orchestration. The Studios remain application-level services rather than becoming inseparable platform components.

sections.heading_text: 30. Proof of Concept — Three Independent Deployments
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-021 > 30. Proof of Concept — Three Independent Deployments
sections.content:
The strongest POC is not a diagram; it is three separate deployments that are intentionally operated with the other two turned off.

Deploy Data Studio alone with an industrial CSV/Parquet/time-series dataset.

Demonstrate compilation, profiling, DAG, preparation and visualization.

Expose the prepared dataset via its API.

Stop ML Studio and Agentic Studio completely; Data Studio must remain functional.

Deploy ML Studio alone with an externally prepared dataset satisfying the Dataset/Feature Contract.

Train/evaluate, select a model and expose inference.

Stop Data Studio; ML Studio must remain functional.

Deploy Agentic Studio with an external REST/MQTT data source.

Create an agent and run a tool/monitoring workflow.

Stop Data Studio and ML Studio; Agentic Studio must remain functional for capabilities not requiring them.

Connect all three through contracts and demonstrate the enhanced end-to-end workflow.

Change and redeploy only one Studio while the other two remain live.

tables:
| Test | Expected evidence | Pass condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data-only | Working Data API + visualization | No ML/Agent dependency |
| ML-only | Working inference endpoint | No Data Studio process |
| Agent-only | Working agent/tool run | No ML/Data Studio process |
| Contract integration | Manifest/model/agent IDs resolved | No private DB access |
| Independent release | One image/version changes | Other services unaffected |
| Independent rollback | One Studio rollback | Others remain available |
| Failure isolation | Stop one Studio | Other supported services continue |
| Scale isolation | Scale one service | Other replicas unchanged |
| Edge deployment | Run chosen Studio on edge | Cloud not required for local capability |
| Tenant isolation | Cross-tenant tests | All unauthorized requests rejected |

sections.content: This modularity directly supports industrial procurement. A plant that only needs data organization and mathematical visualization can purchase/deploy Data Studio as a service. A process engineering group can consume ML Studio's training or inference API. An operations group can consume Agentic Studio for alarms, monitoring and tool orchestration. The enterprise can later join them without replacing the earlier deployments.
tables:
| Industrial scenario | Minimal product | Upgrade path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data historian modernization | Data Studio | Add ML → Agentic |
| Condition monitoring | Data Studio + ML inference | Add Agentic alerts |
| Predictive maintenance | Data + ML | Add Agentic toolkit |
| No-ML process analytics | Data Studio | Remain Data-only |
| Operations automation | Agentic + external APIs | Add ML when required |
| Fleet model serving | ML Studio | Add Agentic monitoring |

sections.content:
It does not mean duplicating identity, policy and telemetry in three incompatible ways.

It does not mean each Studio has a separate user experience with no common Jane experience.

It does not mean arbitrary direct database access.

It does not mean every Studio must ship every dependency.

It does not mean the Studios cannot cooperate.

It means cooperation is explicit, replaceable and contract-driven.

A Studio may depend on another Studio's CONTRACT, but must not depend on another Studio's INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION.

GOOD:ML Studio → GET /v1/data/{dataset}/feature-contractBAD:ML Studio → SELECT * FROM data_studio.internal_feature_tableGOOD:Agentic Studio → POST /v1/models/{model}/inferBAD:Agentic Studio → import ml_studio.private.training.pipeline

sections.content:
The Twelve-Factor methodology supports explicit dependencies, configuration separation, backing-service abstraction, build/release/run separation and independently runnable service processes. citeturn0search7turn0search1

CNCF's cloud-native principles describe loosely coupled, observable, manageable services and emphasize lifecycle management, probes, resource controls, permissions and fault-aware deployment. citeturn0search0

CNCF's cloud-native reference architecture explicitly describes applications as distributable and built from loosely coupled services, each performing a single function. citeturn0search10

CNCF edge-native guidance adds autonomy, capability sensitivity, data persistence and edge operations—important when AI-ConneX Studios are independently deployed into plants. citeturn0search6

ONNX Runtime provides a portable inference layer across different source frameworks and hardware/software stacks, supporting cloud, edge and mobile deployment. citeturn0search2turn0search8

The result is a modular AI-ConneX architecture: three independent industrial products that become significantly more powerful when composed, without becoming technically inseparable.
